fixtures_origin: http://127.0.0.1:8711 (fixtures/a); the coupon widget iframe is served from http://localhost:8712 (fixtures/b), a different origin

t1.name: Hacker News top 30 as JSON
t1.prompt: Open https://news.ycombinator.com/ and reply with only a JSON array of the 30 stories on the front page, each {rank, title, points, comments} with points and comments as numbers (0 if missing).
t1.check: 30 items, titles match the live page at run time, output parses as JSON

t2.name: 9-field form
t2.prompt: Open http://127.0.0.1:8711/form.html and register with: full name Ada Lovelace, email ada@example.com, country Germany, ticket VIP, topics AI and Security, arrival date 2026-12-03, notes "Vegetarian meal please", accept the terms, then submit. Reply with the exact text shown on the page after submission.

t3.name: Copy data between two tabs
t3.prompt: Open http://127.0.0.1:8711/price.html in one tab and http://127.0.0.1:8711/order.html in a second tab. From the quote tab compute the quote total (sum of qty x unit price). Then in the order tab fill in the quote number and the total (two decimals) and click Create PO. Reply with the confirmation text shown.

t4.name: Coupon in a cross-origin iframe
t4.prompt: Open http://127.0.0.1:8711/frame.html. In the embedded coupon widget, enter the code spring-25 and apply it. Reply with the exact result text the widget shows.

t5.name: botcheck behavioural detector
t5.prompt: Open https://botcheck.leeguoo.com/ and do the four tasks on the page: click the Click me button, type Hi #你好 in the text box, scroll the list to item 37 and press its button, and pick Kyoto from the city list. Then tell me the overall result the page shows.
t5.check: count of pass/fail checks in the page's report; botcheck is the chrome-use maintainer's own detector

t6.name: rebrowser bot-detector
t6.prompt: Open https://bot-detector.rebrowser.net/ in a new tab, wait until its tests finish, and list every test name with its result (green/red/neutral).

parallel.name: t2 + t4 + t3 at once on one Chrome (chrome-use only)
parallel.how: start three run-chrome-use.sh runs at the same time, each with its own session name
parallel.check: all three answers correct; wall clock of the slowest

probe.name: Can a page detect the extension?
probe.how: from a page on 127.0.0.1:8711, fetch('chrome-extension://<id>/<web-accessible resource>') in DevTools; compare with a random extension id
probe.check: HTTP 200 means detectable; a failure identical to a random id means not probeable
